claims.statement: An external client app has a Consumer Key and an optional Consumer Secret that a developer copies from the app settings after verifying their identity; the secret is needed only where the app specifies that the Web Server Flow requires it.

sources.supports: Depending on whether you’ve specified that it’s required, also copy the Consumer Secret.
sources.locator: Create an External Client App in Your Org: consumer key and secret steps

sources.supports: If you specified in the external client app that the Web Server Flow requires a client (consumer) secret, the command prompts you for it.
sources.locator: Create an External Client App in Your Org: closing paragraphs

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: This candidate is recorded at existence level only: the pages read state no prefix, length, alphabet or separator for the consumer secret, and do not say whether a connected app consumer secret has the same or a different shape. Is the connected-app consumer secret a separate family, and what does either look like? One open-source scanner rule artifact (TruffleHog, read 2026-10-04) matches a consumer secret only near a salesforce/consumer/secret keyword; a single artifact does not corroborate, so it stays a lead and no shape is recorded.
